problem:
| $x$ | **$1$** | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-20$ | $-10$ | $40$ | $20$ | $10$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as 

$$
[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}]=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y,
$$

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $y$ is the observation vector. Which of the following is the observation vector $y$ in this context?

examples.knowledge_point: Identifying the Elements of a Polynomial Regression Model
examples.problem:
| $x$ | **$2$** | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** | **$6$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $40$ | $70$ | $120$ | $100$ | $80$ |

The vector of coefficients of the curve $y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x + \beta_2 x^2 + \beta_3 x^3$ that best fits the data above can be found using polynomial regression as

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14072333/assets/93a2e368924ac5d892ce203e2b2c2ee0007ebb30bb71476272385d5b26695113.png)

where $X$ is the corresponding design matrix and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector. Find $X$ and $\mathbf{y}$ in this context.
examples.worked_solution:
| $x$ | **$\color{blue}2$** | **$\color{blue}3$** | **$\color{blue}4$** | **$\color{blue}5$** | **$\color{blue}6$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $\color{red}40$ | $\color{red}70$ | $\color{red}120$ | $\color{red}100$ | $\color{red}80$ |

The coefficients of the curve

$$
y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x + \beta_2 x^2 + \beta_3 x^3
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution ${\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}}$ to the system

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{X}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & {2}^{2} & {2}^{3} \\ 1 & 3 & {3}^{2} & {3}^{3} \\ 1 & 4 & {4}^{2} & {4}^{3} \\ 1 & 5 & {5}^{2} & {5}^{3} \\ 1 & 6 & {6}^{2} & {6}^{3}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{\beta }{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2} \\ {\beta }_{3}\end{aligned}]}} & =\overset{y}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}40 \\ 70 \\ 120 \\ 100 \\ 80\end{aligned}]}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta$ is the parameter vector, and $\mathbf{y}$ is the observation vector.

feedback.problem:
| $x$ | **$3$** | **$4$** | **$5$** | **$6$** | **$7$** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-2$ | $2$ | $0$ | $2$ | $-3$ |

Consider the data above and the matrices below. Find an expression for the vector of coefficients of the curve $y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}$ that best fits the data. 

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & {3}^{2} \\ 1 & 4 & {4}^{2} \\ 1 & 5 & {5}^{2} \\ 1 & 6 & {6}^{2} \\ 1 & 7 & {7}^{2}\end{aligned}],\,\beta =[\begin{aligned}{\beta }_{0} \\ {\beta }_{1} \\ {\beta }_{2}\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ 0 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
The coefficients of the curve 

$$
y={\beta }_{0}+{\beta }_{1}x+{\beta }_{2}{x}^{2}
$$

that best fits the data can be found as the least-squares solution $\overset{^}{\beta }$ to the system 

$$
X\beta =y,
$$

where $X$ is the design matrix, $\beta $ is the parameter vector, and $y$ is the observation vector.

Pre-multiplying this equation by ${X}^{T},$ we obtain the corresponding normal equation

$$
{X}^{T}\,X\overset{^}{\beta }={X}^{T}y.
$$

Since the columns of $X$ are linearly independent, the matrix ${X}^{T}X$ is invertible and 

$$
\overset{^}{\beta }=({X}^{T}\,X)^{-1}{X}^{T}y.
$$
